The Keeper's Notes

These notes were typed on an old machine that wrapped every line at about
seventy characters, so each paragraph arrives broken into several short
lines that belong together. The Reader should join them back into one
flowing paragraph without losing a single word.

A word split at the end of a line, like the word lamp-
lighter here, should come back together. A name such as Anne-
Marie keeps its hyphen.

Things to pack for the night watch:
- a flask of tea
- two spare wicks
- the logbook and a pencil

The sea is calm tonight,
The tide is full, the moon lies fair
Upon the straits.

Last paragraph of the notes.
